abstract: The Digital Education Council's AI in Higher Education Global Survey 2026 (July 9, 2026) draws on 45,398 responses from 27,284 students and 18,114 faculty across 35 countries. 88% of students use AI in learning; 77% of faculty use it in teaching (+16pp YoY). Faculty intent to use AI in teaching dropped in US/Canada to 67% (lowest globally) while other regions run 89-94%.
keyFindings: 88% of students use AI in learning; 77% of faculty use AI in teaching
Faculty AI use up 16 percentage points from 2025 to 2026
45,398 total responses across 27,284 students and 18,114 faculty in 35 countries
57% of students report inadequate AI guidance in assessments; only 29% believe instructors are equipped to guide them
Faculty AI-use intent in US/Canada dropped from 76% to 67% — lowest globally
methodology: Global online survey of students and faculty across 35 countries fielded in first half of 2026 by the Digital Education Council.
qualifiers: DEC is a self-appointed industry council with commercial interests in AI-in-education tooling. Survey is opt-in, so likely over-represents AI-engaged students and faculty. Adoption signal is strong; displacement is not directly measured.
